hints: The final throw can be 1 through 6, so a way to make sum s can come from sums s-1 through s-6.
Let dp[0]=1 for the one way to make zero with no throws.
For each sum, add the counts for legal last-face values and reduce modulo 1,000,000,007.
analogy: Choose the last die face; the earlier throws must make exactly what remains.
example: For n=3: ways are 1+1+1, 1+2, 2+1, and 3, so dp[3]=4.
correctness: Every nonempty sequence of throws has one unique last face, and removing it leaves one sequence for a smaller sum; this partitions all solutions.
complexity: O(6n)=O(n) time and O(n) space, where n is the target sum.
algorithm: Set dp[0]=1. For each sum s=1..n, add dp[s-d] for die faces d=1..6 with s>=d, modulo 1,000,000,007. dp[s] counts ordered sequences of throws that total s.
